amendments.normalized_body: In `emit_molt_failure` (shrimp.rs ~line 1380-1381), the `critical_gh_failure` computation lacks the `params.gh_min_d > 0.0` guard that was added to `critical_gh_deficit` in `molt_cycle` (line 554-555). When `gh_min_d == 0.0` (user disables GH minimum), the event path computes `gh_ratio = 0/0.01 = 0` which falsely triggers `critical_gh_failure`, emitting a misleading "critical GH ratio 0.00<0.30" detail instead of the correct "score X<Y" form. Fix: add the same `params.gh_min_d > 0.0 &&` guard to line 1381, i.e. `let critical_gh_failure = params.gh_min_d > 0.0 && gh_ratio < params.critical_molt_gh_ratio;`

[medium] `temp_condition_min_factor` is validated as a normal unit-interval runtime parameter, so `0.0` and values below `0.01` are allowed ([crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:466-469]). But `molt_cycle` immediately overrides that configuration with a hardcoded `0.01` cadence floor at [crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:557-559], and then uses that floored value to schedule readiness at [crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:632]. In practice, a preset that intentionally sets `temp_condition_min_factor = 0.0` still forces molts every `base_interval / 0.01` days, which can keep generating failed molts, `failed_molt_accum`, and mortality even though the named parameter says cadence support should be zero. Either reject `< 0.01` in validation or make the cadence path honor the configured floor exactly.

[medium] The new hard-fail guard in `molt_cycle` correctly disables critical-GH failure when `gh_min_d == 0.0` ([crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:554-555]), and `gh_min_d = 0.0` is explicitly valid at runtime ([crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:333-339]). But `emit_molt_failure` still unconditionally computes `gh_ratio = gh_d / max(gh_min_d, 0.01)` and emits `critical GH ratio ...` whenever that synthetic ratio is below the threshold ([crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1380-1440]). That means a zero-GH-floor configuration can produce failure events that blame a critical GH ratio even though the resolution logic did not use GH as a hard-fail cause. Gate the diagnostic with the same `gh_min_d > 0.0` condition so the event stream stays truthful.
